answer: DeepWalk learns vertex embeddings by first doing unsupervised random-walk-based representation learning, then using a supervised objective for node classification that directly optimizes the embeddings to predict node labels. This helps because the learned vectors are not only good at preserving local graph co-occurrence structure, but are also adjusted to separate classes in the embedding space. Compared with many other deep learning methods that learn graph features indirectly or require more hand-engineered input, DeepWalk’s supervised fine-tuning makes the latent embeddings more discriminative for classification and typically improves downstream node-label prediction performance.
